parts.title: Model Government Day
parts.text: The civics class held its annual model government day, and Henrik, Layne, and Ismail landed in a mock legislature. Their task was to pass **legislation** creating a recycling program for the school. Layne urged both parties in the room to cooperate, since a **bipartisan** bill backed by members of each side would last longer than one squeaking by on a single vote. Before debate began, every party held a **caucus**, a private meeting to settle on a strategy.

parts.title: Debate and Delay
parts.text: The opposition party formed a **coalition** with a small group of independents, hoping to win a majority. Ismail, one of those independents, chose to **abstain** on the first vote, refusing to take a side until he understood the costs. Another member tried a **filibuster**, speaking about lunch trays for twenty minutes to delay the vote, until the teacher pointed to the time limit in the rules.

parts.title: Checks and Balances
parts.text: A student panel provided **oversight**, making sure the legislature followed its own rules. Layne explained that a real legislature can **impeach** an official accused of serious wrongdoing, though removal is rare and requires a formal trial. The class also studied an old court case that set a **precedent** later judges followed. Finally, the legislature let each grade keep its **autonomy** over its own recycling bins and sent the plan to a **referendum**, so the whole **electorate** of students could vote directly.

parts.title: A Long Conversation
parts.text: The plan passed, though not by much. Henrik noticed that no single speech had decided everything; the process asked for patience, cooperation, and respect for the rules. Ismail said democracy felt less like a contest and more like a long conversation in which every voice gets a chance to be heard.

definitions.meaning1: Supported by members of two political parties. Example: The bridge repair bill was bipartisan, passing with votes from both parties.
definitions.studentChallenge: The ___ committee had equal numbers of members from each party.

definitions.meaning1: To formally charge a public official with serious wrongdoing. Example: The legislature voted to impeach the governor over the accusations.
definitions.meaning2: To question the honesty of a witness. Example: The lawyer tried to impeach the witness by pointing out earlier contradictions.
definitions.studentChallenge: A legislature may vote to ___ an official accused of misusing public money.

definitions.meaning1: Laws, or a proposed law, made by a governing body. Example: New legislation requires every bicycle sold in the state to have lights.
definitions.meaning2: The process of making laws. Example: Legislation can take months of research, debate, and compromise.
definitions.studentChallenge: The council passed new ___ to protect the town's river from pollution.

definitions.meaning1: A direct vote by all the people on a single question. Example: The town held a referendum to decide whether to build a new library.
definitions.studentChallenge: Voters will decide the question of the new stadium in this month's ___.

definitions.meaning1: The freedom to govern or make decisions for oneself. Example: The club had the autonomy to choose its own projects.
definitions.studentChallenge: Teenagers often crave more ___ as they grow older, wanting to make their own choices.

definitions.meaning1: A meeting of members of a political party or group to choose a strategy or candidate. Example: The party held a caucus to choose its nominee.
definitions.meaning2: A group within a legislature united by a shared interest. Example: The environmental caucus pushed for cleaner rivers.
definitions.studentChallenge: Before the debate, the party members met in a private ___ to agree on a plan.

definitions.meaning1: An alliance of groups or parties joining together for a common goal. Example: Several small parties formed a coalition to win a majority.
definitions.studentChallenge: Local groups built a broad ___ to push for cleaner rivers.

definitions.meaning1: To choose not to vote or take part. Example: She decided to abstain because she had not studied both candidates.
definitions.meaning2: To hold back from something, such as a food or habit. Example: He chose to abstain from sugar for a month.
definitions.studentChallenge: If you do not know enough about an issue, it may be wiser to ___ from voting.

definitions.meaning1: All the people who are eligible to vote in an election. Example: The electorate turned out in record numbers on election day.
definitions.studentChallenge: Candidates spend months trying to win the trust of the ___.

definitions.meaning1: An earlier action or decision that serves as an example or guide for later ones. Example: The court's ruling set a precedent that later judges followed.
definitions.studentChallenge: The committee had no ___ to follow, so it created its own procedure.

definitions.meaning1: A long speech or other tactic used to delay a vote in a legislature. Example: The senator launched a filibuster to delay the final vote.
definitions.meaning2: To delay a vote by making long speeches. Example: Senators may filibuster by talking for hours.
definitions.studentChallenge: The minority party used a ___ to keep the bill from reaching a vote.

definitions.meaning1: The act of watching over an activity or organization to make sure it is run properly. Example: An independent board provides oversight of the city's spending.
definitions.meaning2: A mistake made by failing to notice something. Example: Leaving her name off the list was an oversight.
definitions.studentChallenge: Without proper ___, the agency could waste public money.

secretPassage.instructions: Read the passage below. Fill in each blank with the correct vocabulary word from the word bank.
secretPassage.passage:
Henrik's report followed an imaginary bill through the town of Riverbend. The proposed _(1)_ would pay for repairs to three old bridges. Members of the mayor's party first met in a _(2)_ to choose their strategy. Because they lacked a majority, they negotiated a _(3)_ deal that members of the opposing party could also support. A small group of independents agreed to join them in a _(4)_, and together they had enough votes.

One council member tried a _(5)_ by reading old budget reports aloud for hours, hoping to delay the vote. Another chose to _(6)_, declining to vote either way because of a conflict of interest. After the bill passed, a citizens' board provided _(7)_ to make sure the money was spent properly. If an official misused the funds, the council could _(8)_ that person and begin removal proceedings.

Henrik noted that an earlier decision to rebuild the library had created a _(9)_ that guided the council this time. He also found that each neighborhood kept its _(10)_, the freedom to choose its own small projects like parks. Finally, the largest cost would be settled in a _(11)_, a direct vote, so the whole _(12)_ of Riverbend could decide.
